The project plan was not to influence internal policies but to provide skills to the WROs/As to engage in advocacy and lobbying for law and legal reforms and to link them to national and regional advocacy platforms available to support their advocacy work.

Regional-wise, WCW has had a major influence on governmental decisions. The work of the consortium in South Sudan and Uganda has resulted in substantial developments, including support for the passage of thorough family laws. Their interaction with the CEDAW Committee and later recommendations have brought attention to urgent problems and suggested local legal system improvements. Moreover, the third Women's Rights Cluster Report's submission to the UN Human Rights Council's UPR mechanism demanded the long-delayed Family Bill (Marriage and Divorce Bill, 2009), changes to the Penal Code Act to widen the definition of rape, and fast-tracking of the National Legal Aid Bill (2020).

The project plan was not to influence internal policies but to provide skills to the WROs/As to engage in advocacy and lobbying for law and legal reforms and to link them to national and regional advocacy platforms available to support their advocacy work.

Year 1 focused on the development of a manual for capacity strengthening called the Feminist Paricipatory Manual, which was followed by a ToT in 2022 and rolled out in 2022/2023 across the countries (Sudan, Ethiopia, South Sudan, Uganda, and the Somalia Region) among the coalition members established in 2021.

Support South Sudan to ratify Maputo Protocol and South Sudan FIDA to submit their shadow report to the CEDAW Committee, which was due in 2022

Through the Africa Family Law Network, the WCW has been instrumental in supporting family law reform throughout many nations. Involving three other area groups, this cooperative effort has sponsored several advocacy projects. Especially in South Sudan, the consortium's October 2021 shadow report and two oral presentations before the CEDAW Committee resulted in the Committee's concluding observations, including their recommendations. Emphasizing women's rights—including those of Muslim women—along with abolishing child and forced marriage as well as fighting violence against women and girls, the shadow report focused Likewise, in Uganda, a shadow report sent in March 2022, along with oral comments, produced five consortium proposals included in the Committee's concluding observations. The regional network also supported South Sudan during Maputo's 20 celebrations to push for its ratification without reservations.

Support Sudan to continue monitoring the implementation of the NAP that was developed after the ratification of the Maputo Protocol. Also, support South Sudan in the implementation of the revitalized agreements.

comment.narrative: These are the WROs/WCW Partners SIHA engaged with to advance the rights of women and gender equality

The project highlighted the gendered impacts of political conflict, including enforced disappearances and conflict-related sexual violence. SIHA Network used global and regional platforms, such as the 81st ACHPR and CSW68, to advocate for women’s inclusion in peacebuilding and informal justice processes, raising visibility of women’s and girls’ experiences in conflict-affected areas. At the regional level, WCW consortium members organized side events addressing gender justice, childhood and early forced marriage, adolescent mothers’ social protection, and GBV. SIHA also issued a public statement on the deteriorating human rights situation, particularly in Sudan.
